title_en: The ruling on more than one call to prayer
body_ar:
إذا كان الحي له مؤذن راتب يؤذن في مكبر يسمع من أقصى الحي فما حكم أذان غيره بعده هل هو سنة أو جائز أو هو تعد على وظيفة الغير؟

أن تعدد الأذان مشروع في الجمعة وفي صلاة الفجر، وفي صلاة الفجر يسن أن يؤذن من السدس الأخير من الليل ليقوم النائم ويغتسل الجنب ويتأهب الناس للصلاة، ويسن كذلك أذان ثان عند طلوع الفجر ليعلم الناس أن الفجر قد دخل فيكفوا عن المفطرات إذا أرادوا الصوم ويصلوا كذلك، وقد صح عن النبي (ص) أنه قال: «إن بلالا يؤذن بليل فلا يمنعن أحدكم طعامه وشرابه حتى يؤذن ابن أم مكتوم فإنه رجل ضرير لا يؤذن حتى يقال له: أصبحت أصبحت..

وقد رتبهما رسول الله (ص) لأذان الفجر، كذلك الجمعة فإن عثمان رضي الله عنه رتب لها مؤذنا يؤذن قبل وقتها ومؤذنا يؤذن عندما يجلس الإمام على المنبر، وأراد بذلك إعلام الناس ليتأهبوا للجمعة لأنها أيضا تحتاج إلى تهيئة وغسل وتطيب ونظافة فيحتاج ذلك إلى وقت وإذا لم يسمعوا الأذان إلا وقد جلس الإمام على المنبر فاتهم خير كثير، وأما غير ذلك من الصلوات فإنما يشرع تعدد الأذان فيه إذا كان الذين يسمعون الأذان الثاني غير الذين سمعوا الأول، مثل ما كان الحال في مسجد الكوفة في زمان علي رضي الله عنه، فقد كان له أربعة مؤذنين يؤذنون على أطراف المسجد لكن الذي يسمع هذا غير الذي يسمع هذا، وذلك لاتساع المسجد فقد كان يعلق فيه مائة ألف سيف، في اسطواناته، فلذلك كان المسجد متسعا جدا يصلي فيه مائة ألف مقاتل، فلهذا الذين يسمعون صوت المؤذن في الناحية الشرقية غير الذين يسمعونه في الناحية الغربية وهكذا، ومع هذا فلا ينكر تعدد الأذان ولو سمع الناس بعضه لأن أهل الشام في زمان معاوية رضي الله عنه كان لهم مؤذنون يؤذنون دفعة ولم يكن الجامع الأموي بهذا القدر من الضخامة كحال جامع الكوفة، وإن كان كبيرا أيضا لكن لم يكن بهذه الضخامة في ذلك الوقت.
body_en:
If a neighbourhood has a regular muezzin who gives the call to prayer over a loudspeaker that is heard from the farthest part of the neighbourhood, what is the ruling on someone else giving the call after him? Is it a sunnah, or permissible, or is it an encroachment on another man's office?

More than one call to prayer is sanctioned in the Sharia (mashrūʿ) for the Friday prayer and for the Fajr prayer. In the Fajr prayer it is recommended (sunnah) that the call be given in the last sixth of the night, so that the sleeper may rise, the one in a state of major ritual impurity may perform the full ritual washing (ghusl), and people may prepare themselves for the prayer. It is likewise recommended that there be a second call at the breaking of dawn, so that people may know that Fajr has entered and may therefore hold back from the things that break the fast if they intend to fast, and may pray. It is soundly established from the Prophet, upon whom be peace, that he said: "Bilal gives the call while it is still night, so let none of you be kept from his food and his drink until Ibn Umm Maktum gives the call, for he is a blind man who does not call until he is told: 'You have entered upon the morning, you have entered upon the morning'.."

The Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, appointed the two of them for the call to Fajr. Likewise for the Friday prayer: ʿUthman, may God be pleased with him, appointed for it a muezzin who called before its time and a muezzin who called when the imam sat upon the pulpit. By this he intended to inform the people so that they might prepare themselves for the Friday prayer, since it too requires preparation, washing, applying perfume and cleanliness, and that takes time; and if they were not to hear the call until the imam had already sat upon the pulpit, much good would escape them. As for the other prayers, more than one call is prescribed in them only where those who hear the second call are other than those who heard the first — as was the case in the mosque of Kufa in the time of ʿAli, may God be pleased with him. It had four muezzins who called from the edges of the mosque, but the one who heard this one was not the one who heard that one, because of the mosque's great extent: a hundred thousand swords used to be hung in it, on its columns. The mosque was therefore very large indeed, and a hundred thousand fighting men prayed in it; so those who heard the muezzin's voice on the eastern side were other than those who heard him on the western side, and so on. Even so, more than one call is not to be condemned even if the people hear only part of it, because the people of Syria in the time of Muʿawiyah, may God be pleased with him, had muezzins who called all at once, and the Umayyad Mosque was not of that degree of vastness as the mosque of Kufa was — although it too was large, it was not of that vastness at that time.

flags.arabic: هل هو سنة أو جائز أو هو تعد على وظيفة الغير؟
flags.context: the third limb of the question — whether a second call encroaches on the appointed muezzin's office
options: leave the question's third limb unanswered, as the source does
add an editorial note on the page that the third limb is not addressed
suppress the third limb from the displayed question
flags.note: The Sheikh answers when more than one call is sanctioned, and says at the end that it 'is not to be condemned'. He does not address in terms whether it encroaches on the appointed muezzin's office, which is what the questioner asked about his own neighbourhood. A reader may take the closing sentence as a ruling on that point. Option 2 would alter the source and is not recommended.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.

The date shown by the CMS (27 December 2010) is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.
'Sanctioned in the Sharia (mashrūʿ)' is used for mashrūʿ, which states that the Sharia provides for the act; it is not one of the five rulings and must not be read as 'recommended' or 'obligatory'.
The closing double dot inside the hadith of Bilal is in the source. The received wording of that report continues beyond this point; nothing has been supplied.
'A hundred thousand swords ... a hundred thousand fighting men' is the Sheikh's own report about the mosque of Kufa and is translated as given, without comment on its historicity.
